title: The AGN fuelling/feedback cycle in nearby radio galaxies - IV. Molecular gas conditions and jet-ISM interaction in NGC 3100
question: Investigate the molecular gas physical conditions, kinematics, and jet-ISM interaction in the nearby low-excitation radio galaxy NGC 3100 using multiple molecular transitions and continuum data.

recipe.goal: Create moment maps of molecular lines
recipe.method: Masked moment technique: copy of cleaned cube is Gaussian-smoothed spatially (FWHM equal to synthesized beam) and Hanning-smoothed in velocity; a 3D mask is defined above a flux threshold, then applied to the un-smoothed cube.
key_parameters: Flux threshold = 1.2 sigma (measured in un-smoothed cube)

recipe.goal: Extract spectral profiles, line widths, and integrated fluxes / upper limits
recipe.method: Extract spectra within boxes covering central 10"x11" (CO) and 1.5"x1.5" (HCO+); measure FWZI across channels >=3 sigma; measure CO FWHM directly from double-horned profile and HCO+ FWHM via Gaussian fit; compute 3-sigma upper limits for non-detections.
key_parameters: Extraction box: 10" x 11" for CO, 1.5" x 1.5" for HCO+(4-3); FWZI threshold >= 3 sigma
assumptions: For SiO and HNCO upper limits, emission is assumed unresolved (within synthesized beam) with expected FWHM = 340 km s^-1 (same as CO(2-1)).

recipe.goal: Estimate total molecular gas mass from CO(1-0)
recipe.method: Convert integrated CO(1-0) flux density to total molecular gas mass including heavy elements using the standard Bolatto et al. (2013) relation.
assumptions: Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor X_CO = 2 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (with +/- 0.4 dex systematic scatter), z = 0.0088, D_L = 38.0 Mpc (10% distance uncertainty).

recipe.goal: Compute spatially-resolved line ratio maps (R_21, R_31, R_HCO)
recipe.method: Re-image CO cubes to identical channel number, channel width, pixel and image size, select a common uv range, convolve to a common 1.4" x 0.9" beam, produce masked moment 0 maps, and divide using CASA immath.
key_parameters: Common beam: 1.4" x 0.9"; channel width: 10 km s^-1 (for CO ratios) and 105 km s^-1 (for HCO+/CO(2-1) ratio)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and optically thin conditions in the inner high-ratio region to infer T_ex >= 50 K from R_31 >= 12.

recipe.goal: 3D kinematic modelling of CO(3-2) and outflow mass/rate estimation
recipe.method: Simulate mock cubes with KinMS using a nuclear two-armed logarithmic spiral embedded in an axisymmetric exponential disc, linear radial PA and inclination warps, an arctangent rotation curve, and spatially constant velocity dispersion; fit to observed cube with KinMS_MCMC; extract spectra in velocity residual regions to identify inflow/outflow components and compute outflow mass and rate.
key_parameters: 10^5 - 10^6 point-like sources; R_max = 300 pc, v_max = 200 km s^-1 for outflow
assumptions: Pure circular motion for the baseline model; spatially constant intrinsic velocity dispersion; optically thin LTE gas with T_ex = 50 K giving X_CO = 2.5 x 10^19 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 for outflow mass; spherical geometry for outflow rate (M_dot <= 3 v_max M_out / R_max).

recipe.goal: Fit radio to (sub-)mm continuum spectral energy distribution
recipe.method: Fit single power-law function S_nu = A nu^alpha to total, core, and jet continuum flux densities across radio and ALMA mm bands.
assumptions: Radio source is compact with no emission on larger scales, allowing combination of low- and high-resolution data for total spectrum; matched-resolution data used for core and jet components.

recipe.goal: Estimate dust mass, molecular gas-to-dust ratio, and gas-phase metallicity
recipe.method: Measure mean extinction <A_lambda> from B-I colour map in regions co-spatial with CO, compute dust mass M_dust = Sigma <A_lambda> Gamma_lambda^-1, and derive gas-phase metallicity upper limit from M_gas/M_dust using the Draine et al. (2007) relation.
assumptions: Milky Way B-band mass absorption coefficient Gamma_B = 8 x 10^-6 mag kpc^2 M_sun^-1; solar metallicity 12+log10(O/H) = 8.66 at gas-to-dust ratio of 100; neglecting HI yields a lower limit on M_gas/M_dust and upper limit on metallicity.
